title: Movie Lovers' Favorite App Letterboxd Might Get a New Owner!
summary: Imagine a social media site just for movie lovers, where you can rate every film you watch, make lists of your favorites, and see what your friends are watching. That's Letterboxd! It's been around for years and has 26 million users, including famous people like Charli XCX and Jack Harlow. Now, Letterboxd is thinking about being sold to a bigger company. The current owner, a Canadian company called Tiny, bought most of Letterboxd in 2023 for $50 million. Now they want to sell it for $250 million—five times more! Several big names are interested: Sony Pictures, Netflix, Paramount, and even Alexis Ohanian, who helped start Reddit. Some investment companies are also in the mix. Why would they want Letterboxd? It's a rare, independent platform that young movie fans really love. It has cool features like the 'Four Favorites' where celebrities share their top four movies, and a video store where you can rent hard-to-find films. But fans are a little nervous. They worry a big company might change Letterboxd too much—maybe add lots of ads, or use it to promote only their own movies. Some people remember how other fun websites changed after being bought. Sony might be a good fit because they've been buying things for movie fans, like the Alamo Drafthouse cinema chain. Netflix and Paramount might have other plans. Nothing is decided yet, and Letterboxd says any decision would involve the founders. For now, movie lovers are watching closely—just like they watch and rate films on the app!
why_it_matters: If Letterboxd is sold, the way you talk about and discover movies with friends could change, just like when other online spaces add ads or new rules—so it's important to pay attention to the services you love.

background_read: Letterboxd (a movie-tracking app launched in 2011) has grown to 26 million users by letting film fans log, rate, and discuss movies in a community-driven way.
The company Tiny, based in Canada, specializes in buying small tech startups and helping them expand; they originally acquired Letterboxd in 2023 for $50 million.

In the tech world, when a popular app like Letterboxd is sold to a much larger company like Netflix or Sony, fans often worry that the original simple charm might be lost in favor of ads or content promotion.
Article_Structure: WHO: Letterboxd (a movie-rating social app) and its current owner Tiny, plus potential buyers such as Sony Pictures, Netflix, Paramount, and Alexis Ohanian.
WHAT: Tiny is considering selling Letterboxd for $250 million, sparking interest from several major entertainment and tech companies.
WHERE: The deal would happen in the business world, involving the Canadian parent company Tiny and big Hollywood and streaming giants.
WHY: Tiny hopes to earn a large profit from the sale, while buyers see Letterboxd as a way to connect with a dedicated audience of young, movie-loving fans.

perspectives.description: They love the app's clean, ad-free design and quirky features, and they worry that a big company might ruin it with intrusive ads or biased content promotion.
